parsed.attack: A one-time purchase at $25 nets $17.50 after the 30% store fee, and with zero marginal cost that is the entire lifetime value - there is no second payment to amortise acquisition against. Break-even on paid installs therefore needs an install-to-purchase rate of 5.84/17.50 = 33% on iOS and 1.92/17.50 = 11% on Android, against a realistic 1-3%; at 2% the cost per paying user is $292 on iOS and $96 on Android for a $17.50 product, 5-17x underwater. Raising the price does not rescue it - $49 still needs 17% iOS conversion - and the 8% refund kill line shaves the $17.50 further. Every channel except free word of mouth is arithmetically closed.
parsed.strongest_defence: Zero marginal cost means every organic sale is pure margin: with roughly 13M US households on private wells and 20M+ on septic, the shareable house sheet handed to a contractor or a buyer is a free distribution loop, and a $25 one-off never needs a purchased install to be profitable.
parsed.verdict_reason: The margin side is perfect but a $17.50 net one-time sale cannot repay even an Android install at any realistic conversion rate, so 100% of growth must be organic.
